newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-San Diego could lose Super Bowl - report.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-San Diego could lose Super Bowl - report.

text.p: Should San Diego's plan to expand Jack Murphy Stadium falter, the National Football League could shift the 1998 Super Bowl to Pasadena, Calif., according to a published report on Tuesday.

"We are talking to the Rose Bowl (in Pasadena) on a contingency basis as we speak," NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue said in San Diego on Monday, according to the Los Angeles Times. "I hope this stays a contingency plan. We want to play the game here. (But) we do not want to play the game in a construction site, which is what it would be if construction stops."

Tagliabue said the decision on shifting the Super Bowl to the Rose Bowl could hinge on the decision of a California judge, who has set a February 20 trial date on San Diego's $78 million expansion and renovation of Jack Murphy stadium.
The judge is being asked by opponents of the expansion plan to halt construction until the public votes on the project.
